chapter.title: 2025 G7 Final Compliance Report: Artificial Intelligence for SMEs

commitment_text: Sustain investments in AI adoption programs for SMEs, including support for access to compute and digital infrastructure.

definitions.definition: Continuation of support during the evaluation period.
Reachability, affordability, acceptability, and sufficient quality.

classifications.label: strong
classifications.description: Implemented or funded action directly supporting SME AI adoption.

classifications.label: weak
classifications.description: Indirect, preliminary, short-term, or general AI support.

temporal_conditions: Actions are evaluated in the summit-to-summit period.
attribution_conditions: National and collective action require an explicit attribution policy.
identity_conditions: Announcements and outputs from one underlying instrument may be duplicates.
exclusions: General AI measures without meaningful SME targeting may be weak or excluded.

score_guideline.prose: Two or fewer weak actions or countervailing conduct yields -1; three or four weak actions or up to four strong actions yields 0; five or more strong actions yields +1.

open_questions.question: Does “up to four strong actions” mean zero through four or one through four, and what follows for zero-strong cases?
open_questions.proposed_resolution: Preserve both normalizations as scenarios. The one-to-four reading produces a five-or-more-weak gap; the zero-to-four reading overlaps non-compliance at low weak counts. Resolve only in a named profile.

open_questions.question: Does one counteraction override five or more strong actions?

notes: This inventory is a planning fixture and should be checked against page-anchored source text before approval.
